title: Conductance Bound for Arbitrary Linear Permutations
summary: The conductance lower bound is established for generic linear permutations with high probability, but its extension to every arbitrary linear permutation remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the confusion-diffusion network with a linear permutation over $\text{GF}(2^n)$, determine whether the conductance lower bound established for a generic linear permutation also holds for every arbitrary linear permutation. The existing analysis establishes this lower bound with probability $1-o(1)$ for a random matrix $A\in F^{w\times w}$, for $q=o(|F|)$, with a constant factor depending on $w$, but does not cover non-generic linear permutations. The unresolved task is therefore to prove or refute that the same conductance lower bound holds for arbitrary $\text{GF}(2^n)$-linear permutations.

scope.domain: Mathematical foundations of confusion-diffusion networks, finite-field linear permutations, and conductance.
parameters: F: finite field containing the matrix entries
A: random w-by-w matrix defining the generic linear permutation
w: matrix dimension and parameter controlling the constant factor
q: asymptotic parameter constrained by the field size
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute whether the same conductance lower bound holds for every arbitrary, including non-generic, GF(2^n)-linear permutation.

progress.summary: The source explicitly conjectures that the lower bound for generic linear permutations should carry over to non-generic, arbitrary linear permutations. It states that the existing analysis does not cover this case.
citation_labels: Yevgeniy Dodis et al., Indifferentiability of Confusion-Diffusion Networks
